(1) the number of vertebrate animals used in biomedical research in the United Kingdom has risen by 25 per cent over the past 15 years, with a 40 per cent rise in mice alone; (2) the use of animals is predicted to continue to rise, with a 50 per cent increase in mice by 2005; (3) the rise in mice is largely attributable to an increasing use of knock-out, transgenic and chimeric animals; (4)
the use of animals has been rising in recent years, and is likely to continue to do so, particularly in the use of mice and rats.
